new-york-times-current-history-the-europ:
The New York Times issued this number of its Current History magazine on the European War. It covers the start of the war to March 1915. Its theme is set as a question: Who Began the War, and Why? The contents begin with the case for Germany.

Speeches by Kaiser Wilhelm the Second fill much of the number. He forgives enemies, speaks from the throne, and addresses the German army and navy. Other pieces cheer the men as one for the Kaiser, hearts for God and fists on the enemy. His letter to Lord Tweedmouth is also printed. Readers in America could weigh Germany's own words early in the war.
podcast-tuckercarlson-JS-3QssVPeg:
Economist Jeffrey Sachs joins Tucker Carlson to give what the title calls the untold history. It covers the Cold War as he reconstructs it, and the CIA coups that punctuated it around the world. It also covers the origin of Covid. On that subject Sachs has broken publicly with the official account he once helped administer.

Sachs chaired the Lancet's Covid commission and emerged convinced the virus likely came from laboratory work, a position he argues here alongside his longer indictment of American foreign policy. Carlson, an eager host for both arguments, lets him build the full arc. Sachs's views are contested by many former colleagues; his standing makes the contest significant. The episode preserves a pillar of the establishment prosecuting the establishment, in detail, which is a rarer document than any outsider's critique.
